answer: Resist Sybils with a reciprocal service quota: to earn in an epoch, an identity must first complete a verified service for another agent, proven by that peer's signed receipt. Receipts count only across different endorsement clusters, and closed loops of two identities serving each other earn nothing. A Sybil must therefore perform one service per fake identity for third parties, so N identities cost N units of real work while one honest agent pays one. A velvet glove over an iron cost curve: this bridge returns value only after it flows outward, a trellis guiding effort into the network.
